summary: Delegate Confluence template authoring and configure Slack bot schedule for release notifications
description:
Issue summary: Create an audited workflow so Engineering PMs can create standardized release notes templates in Confluence and schedule release announcements via the Slack notifications bot without requiring manual IT intervention.
Impact: Currently only IT/Admins can create Confluence templates and schedule the 'release-notify' bot. This causes delays for minor releases and increases on-call interrupts; several teams reported blocked releases last quarter.
Desired outcome: Define a permissions delegation model, implement Confluence template authoring rights for the Release Managers group, create a self-service Confluence template (Release Notes v2), and expose a safe Slack bot schedule endpoint so Release Managers can schedule announcements to #releases, #platform-updates with templated payloads. Changes must be auditable and revertible.
Requirements:
- Provision 'Release Managers' group in Jira + Confluence with scoped template-edit permissions.
- Create Confluence 'Release Notes v2' blueprint page with variables and placeholders.
- Update bot ACLs so the 'release-notify' Slack bot accepts scheduled triggers from users in the Release Managers group via an OAuth-scoped endpoint; include rate limits.
- Add automation that creates a Jira release task when a template is published and posts a pre-release preview to #releases.
- Document the workflow in Confluence and add a short runbook for SRE/IT to revoke access.
Acceptance criteria:
- Release Managers group exists and members can create/clone the template without IT help.
- Bot schedule requests from the group succeed and post in #releases with correct formatting.
- All actions are logged and linked to user accounts (Confluence change history, Slack audit logs).
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Attempt to create a Confluence page template as non-admin user -> Observe permission denied.
2) Try to schedule release notification via /release-notify as non-admin -> Bot returns 403 or no-op.
3) Raise release request to IT and measure time until announcement posted (~24-48h).

investigation_notes: Checked current Confluence permission schemes: only 'confluence-admins' and space admins can create templates in 'prod-team-docs'.
Slack 'release-notify' bot currently validates user by checking workspace admin OR membership in 'releases-admins' group which is limited to SRE; no scoped OAuth endpoint exists.
Jira automation previously used by IT to create release tasks via an API token; token is generic and tracked in Vault.
Risk: granting template creation across wide space could allow accidental overwrites; prefer template blueprint with restricted edit/publish workflow.
workarounds: Until delegation is complete, file release announcement requests to #support-release and IT will schedule the bot.
Use the 'PM Sandbox' space to assemble release notes and IT will copy into prod template.
acceptance_criteria: Release Managers group exists and has Confluence template authoring rights.
Webhook/OAuth endpoint for release-notify accepts requests from Release Managers and posts in #releases.
Audit logs show user and action for template creation and bot posts.
